title: SLA & Capacity Intake: Enterprise Dedicated Plan — throughput, GPU class, and scaling policy decisions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Consolidate and triage a recent set of enterprise customer asks related to Dedicated capacity sizing and contractual SLAs. Primary intake items: reserved throughput targets, supported GPU classes (A100/H100/other), autoscaling policy constraints and warm pool requirements, and acceptable latency SLOs at reserved capacity. Goal: produce prioritized, scorable requirements and a proposed negotiation template for sales/CS to use during contract talks. Deliverables: 1) requirements matrix mapping customer tiers to reserved throughput, GPU class options, and latency SLO buckets; 2) recommended defaults and optional add-ons (burst policy, pre-warmed instances, multi-region fallbacks); 3) list of follow-up product/engineering work and rough LOE; 4) a one-page guidance doc for sales/CS to set expectations during procurement.
acceptance_criteria: Create a requirements matrix that covers small/medium/enterprise tiers with reserved throughput (reqs/sec and tokens/sec), recommended GPU classes, and expected latency SLOs
Produce a prioritized backlog of feature work with rough estimates and owner recommendations (e.g., runtime changes, console UX, billing adjustments)
Draft a contract negotiation template with standard SLA targets, breach definitions, and recommended surge/burst options
Obtain agreement from ENG and Reliability leads on feasibility of proposed SLO buckets and autoscaling constraints
Share one-page guidance with Sales and CS and collect at least three customer-side validation responses
comments: 2026-02-24 Maya Chen: Ticket created after synthesis of five inbound customer requests and two AE calls. Early asks are heterogeneous: one fintech customer wants 99.9% p99 latency at reserved capacity; one adtech customer wants guaranteed token throughput for batch embedding jobs; another customer requires H100-class GPUs for a specific model portfolio. Need to normalize asks into common variables.

2026-02-28 Diego Ramos: Initial intake meeting with Sales, AE, and Solutions Engineering. Action items: (1) SE to enumerate max steady-state throughput targets from pilot data; (2) ENG to validate realistic p95/p99 latency targets for A100 vs H100 at common seq lengths; (3) PM to draft matrix and negotiation template.

2026-03-03 Priya Singh (Solutions Eng): Shared pilot dashboard links and steady-state throughput numbers for three customers (links attached). Observed warm-up variability; recommend warm pool for workloads with >1M tokens/day.

2026-03-05 Anya Patel (Reliability): High-level feasibility: We can hit 99.9% p95 for reserved clusters under small/medium committed loads but p99 at 99.9% will require stricter isolation and warm pools. Autoscaling with minimum floor will add cost; proposed options noted in the matrix.

2026-03-08 Diego Ramos: Drafted requirements matrix v0.2 and negotiation template. Dropped into shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.example/dedicated-sla-intake-v0.2. Requested ENG review on kernel-level scheduling changes and potential billing model for reserved throughput.

2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Updated ticket with ENG feedback from ARCH sync. ENG asked to split work items into: runtime kernel/kv-cache optimizations (ENG-3602), autoscale policy and warm pool orchestration (ENG-3550), and console UX to allow per-customer reserved throughput config (DES-210). Marking Planned and requesting estimates in next cycle.

2026-03-10 Diego Ramos: Noted risk: customers asking for mixed GPU classes within a single reserved contract (e.g., H100 for LLM generation + A100 for embeddings). Proposed policy: allow one primary GPU class per reserved pool; multi-GPU contracts become a packaged add-on with higher pricing. Added as negotiation clause.

2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Next steps: (a) finalize matrix and LOE by 2026-03-20; (b) coordinate a customer validation session week of 2026-03-22; (c) create PRD stub linking to ENG tickets and the sales template.
2026-03-10 Diego Ramos: Assigned follow-ups to ENG and Design. Pending: cost model from Finance for reserved throughput pricing and legal review of SLA wording.
